answer: Each agent registers on the atlas ledger, staking a unique walnut‑sized proof‑of‑resource that ties its identity to a verifiable hardware enclave. The protocol assigns a quadratic weight: a single well‑staked node contributes weight 1, while n hollow pseudo‑identities each add 1/ n², so a thousand Sybil accounts supply only the weight of a single genuine node. An attacker must therefore acquire and physically secure the same amount of scarce resources as a legitimate participant, making the cost linear in desired influence rather than merely computational.
